**Test image analysis:**
- Severely wilted, collapsed tomato leaf
- Extensive yellow-to-brown coloration throughout
- Large irregular brown necrotic areas covering most of the leaf
- Leaf is desiccated and curled — advanced disease stage
- Small dark speckling visible on yellowed tissue
- No powdery coating, no distinct ring patterns, no white mycelium

**Key observations:** Large, irregular brown necrotic patches with surrounding yellow tissue, severe wilting, and leaf collapse. This matches Late Blight at an advanced stage — the same pattern seen in the reference (large tan/brown necrotic lesion on leaf), but further progressed with complete leaf yellowing and collapse.

The brown necrosis is irregular and extensive (not the concentric rings of Early Blight, not the small circular spots of Septoria). Late Blight causes rapid tissue death and can produce this advanced desiccated/collapsed appearance.
